# gh-2178: [GOAL] Unbrickable session reads — malformed persisted records quarantine themselves, never crash the run (FormatException on hand-appended obligations_ledger)

## Description

## Goal — Unbrickable session reads (v1, first draft)

One sentence: **fa sessions become unbrickable from persisted input — one malformed record quarantines itself with a named, repairable report instead of crashing every turn.**

Today, a single foreign record with a malformed timestamp bricks a 664 MB session: every turn dies within ~300 ms behind a misclassified "provider error". What changes: every parse site that decodes persisted session bytes routes through one tolerant timestamp parser; a record that fails decode is quarantined (excluded from context building, preserved byte-verbatim in the file) with a one-time report naming file, line, record id, and the raw field value; `fa session repair` gains a scan mode that finds and reports such records. Why now: the 2026-11-13→14 incident below is a real, fully-diagnosed instance of the class — and the class is open-ended (any process that touches the JSONL can land it).

## Incident (2026-11-13 → 2026-11-14) — real; every value below is test data

Session `01a0ca2d-783a-78a0-8217-0533f83f8912` of project `~/git/aiin` (aiin), file `2026-09-22T20-32-52-666532_01a0ca2d-783a-78a0-8217-0533f83f8912.jsonl`, 664,905,120 bytes, 37,467 records, under `~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/--Users-uladzimir-klyshevich-git-aiin--/`.

- **2026-11-13 14:29** — a headless `fa --session <name> --prompt-file /tmp/close_aiin_obligations.md` run (launched from the YoLoIT desktop app) shared the SAME session file with the live interactive instance; it closed 32 `obligations_ledger` obligations.
- **14:35:18** — a synthetic `obligations_ledger` custom record was appended DIRECTLY to the JSONL, bypassing the Session API, with `"timestamp": "2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ"` (line 36,937 of the file).
- **Proof the writer was foreign (NOT fa's session layer):**
  - (a) record id `01a1d4b0-c9b6-709b-80c2-3cd97501a715` is a FULL uuidv7; fa's `generateSessionEntryId` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:161–172` on origin/main) always emits the 8-char uuidv7 TAIL (full uuidv7 only after a 100-collision fallback that never fires in practice); the uuidv7 embedded ms decode to 2026-11-13 14:35:18.198 — the same second as the mangled timestamp;
  - (b) the literal `.fZ` fraction (a strftime-style `.%fZ` typo: local clock digits + literal `f` + `Z`) exists in NO fa tag v1.0.715..v1.0.724, NOT on origin/main, and NOT in the compiled YoLoIT.app AOT snapshot (all greps verified empty);
  - (c) 21 s later (record at line 36,943) the interactive session's own bash tool result shows an agent-side python ledger analysis printing `latest ts 2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ` — python was live on this file inside the agent flow.
- **2026-11-14** — user updated fa 1.0.717 → 1.0.724.
- **11:29:19 boot** — resume SUCCEEDS: the windowed reader parsed only the last 200 records (fa.log: `resume_timing open ... window_records=200 ... has_older=true`); the malformed record at position 36,937 is outside that window → masked at boot.
- **11:29:54 first submit** — `auto-compact start tokens=195030` → compaction walks the full branch (`session.getBranch()`, `lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart:1610`, `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:847`) → `SessionRecord.fromJson` bare `DateTime.parse('2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ')` (`lib/src/session/session_record.dart:165`) → FormatException → rendered as `provider error raw ... FormatException: Invalid date format / 2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_run.dart:255` `_renderProviderError` via `_handleRunError`) → `stop=error` within 300 ms.
- **11:30:12 second submit** — byte-identical crash. EVERY subsequent turn repeats → the 664 MB session is bricked. User-visible clip: `error: FormatException: Invalid date format` / `2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ`.

## Mechanism (one sentence, verbatim)

> A foreign hand-appended session record with a malformed timestamp hits the bare `DateTime.parse` in `SessionRecord.fromJson`, so the auto-compactor's full-branch walk throws a FormatException that surfaces as a provider error and kills every turn — amplified by the boot windowed reader (resume fine, first submit dead), the provider-error misclassification (blames the network/update, not the record), and the absence of any corrupt-record quarantine or repair (`session_repair.dart` fixes tool pairing only).

## Why this framing

- **RETRACTED: "1.0.717 → 1.0.724 regression".** The bare `DateTime.parse` is identical in both tags; the update merely re-opened the session one day after the poison landed. Framing it as a regression sends the fix hunting in the wrong diff. (The retraction is why this card pins against origin/main, not a tag pair.)
- **RETRACTED: "provider/network failure".** The error surfaced through the provider-error renderer (`agent_cli_run.dart:255`), so the user blamed the model endpoint and the update. The failure is 100% local, in fa's own record decode, and reproducible with the network unplugged.
- **RETRACTED: "fix the writer".** Hardening one writer (the incident's python) does nothing for the next one: any process sharing the file can append arbitrary bytes. The reader is the only boundary fa owns (see threat model).
- **Kept: "unbrickable from persisted input".** The end state is about the session surviving its own file, not about any specific poison. Timestamp is the demonstrated instance; the protocol built here (tolerant decode → quarantine → named report → repair) is the shape.

## Architecture

Named protocol **`parseRecordTimestamp`**: one pure function, the ONLY way persisted-input timestamps decode.

```
parseRecordTimestamp(raw: String) → (DateTime, degraded: bool)
  1. strict ISO parse first — EXACTLY the grammar bare DateTime.parse accepts today
     (no widening, no narrowing: offset forms, Z, fractional digits — unchanged)
  2. on FormatException → deterministic placeholder DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(0)
     + degraded=true
  3. NEVER throws — no throwing path exists in the API
```

Call sites (core scope), all on origin/main:

- `lib/src/session/session_record.dart:100` — header `timestamp` (`SessionHeader.fromJson`).
- `lib/src/session/session_record.dart:165` — record `timestamp` (`SessionRecord.fromJson`; the crash site).
- `lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:279` — `parseShallowCustomRecord` raw scan. Note: this site already swallows the exception (`on Object { return null; }`) but its contract is "fall back to full decode" — which lands on the bare parse at `:165` and throws anyway. After this card it degrades in place; the fallback remains for other malformed-prefix classes.

**Quarantine + report** (runtime, read-time only — the file is never rewritten by the reader):

- A record whose timestamp degraded is excluded from context building and branch walks (`getBranch`, `buildContextMessages`) but preserved **byte-verbatim** in the file.
- One-time report per malformed record per process: file path, line number, record id, raw field value (bounded excerpt, single line). Surfaces as a CLI warning + fa.log diagnostic; deduped so a repeated turn cannot spam it.
- If a quarantined record is a tree parent of live records, its children remain usable (the record is treated as absent — the same semantics `repairSessionLedgers` already gives dropped records).

**Repair scan mode** (`fa session repair`):

- Gains a scan/report pass that walks the whole file with the existing line scanner and lists every malformed record (file + line + record id + raw value), including ones outside any boot window.
- Optional surgical fix reuses the byte-verbatim surgery + backup infra from `repairSessionLedgers` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`): original preserved at `<path>.bak`, rotated `.bak` → `.bak1` on a second pass, temp `$path.repairing`, writer-lock guard refused under a live writer.
- Today's repair is conservative by construction (unknown custom types and unparseable lines are KEPT) — which is exactly why the poison record survives a repair pass untouched. The scan mode makes it visible instead.

Flow, before → after:

```
boot (windowed ~200 recs: defaultChunkRecords=200)      submit / auto-compact
        |                                                       |
  WindowedSessionStorage                              compactSession ─ session.getBranch()  (FULL branch)
  last 200 records decode                                     |
        |                                             SessionRecord.fromJson
  poison at line 36,937 OUTSIDE window                        |                     |
  → masked, resume OK                                bare DateTime.parse    parseRecordTimestamp (NEW)
                                                           |                     |
                                                    FormatException      strict ok │ FormatException
                                                           |                |            |
                                                    provider error      exact      placeholder + degraded
                                                    stop=error ~300ms   DateTime          |
                                                           |                |        QUARANTINE: skip context,
                                                           v                v        keep bytes verbatim,
                                                    EVERY turn dies    (unchanged)  1× report (file, line,
                                                                                   id, raw value)
```

Invariants:

- **INV1** — no parse of persisted session bytes may throw across the run boundary. Impossible-by-construction: the throwing API for timestamp decode no longer exists (not "caught somewhere", removed).
- **INV2** — the runtime reader never mutates the session file; the only rewriter is `fa session repair` with `.bak` preservation.
- **INV3** — the quarantine report fires at most once per malformed record per process, regardless of turn count.
- **INV4** — valid timestamps decode to the exact `DateTime` the bare parse produced before (bit-identical; golden REG).

## Capability surface (all persisted-input parse sites → our shape)

| # | Parse site (pinned on origin/main) | Input | Today | This card |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `lib/src/session/session_record.dart:100` | header `timestamp` | bare `DateTime.parse` → FormatException kills resume | `parseRecordTimestamp` + degrade |
| 2 | `lib/src/session/session_record.dart:165` | record `timestamp` | bare parse → FormatException kills every turn (the incident) | `parseRecordTimestamp` + **quarantine + report** |
| 3 | `lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:279` | shallow custom-record raw scan | swallows, falls back to full decode where #2 throws | `parseRecordTimestamp`, degrade in place |
| 4 | `lib/src/providers/quota.dart:97/:101` | gateway JSON `resetsAt` / `updatedAt` | bare parse (network-controlled input) | **second tier**: same parser, degrade |
| 5 | `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:1524` | listing index `createdAtIso` | bare parse | **second tier**: same parser, degrade |

### Tolerant timestamp decode (subject: every persisted/network timestamp fa reads)
Strict-first, deterministic placeholder on failure, never throws. The accepted grammar does not change in either direction (INV4) — this is survivability, not leniency.

### Quarantine + report (subject: malformed session records)
Excluded from context/branch walks; bytes preserved verbatim; one-time named report (file, line, record id, raw value); flood-capped (many poison records → per-record lines up to a cap, then a count summary).

### Repair scan mode (subject: the session file on disk)
Whole-file scan, finds poison outside any window, reports it, optional byte-verbatim surgical fix with `.bak` rotation; refused under a live writer.

### Tiering
- **Core (this card):** sites 1–3, quarantine + report, repair scan mode.
- **Second tier (in-card, opt-in):** sites 4–5 — same-class hardening of sibling bare `DateTime.parse` on untrusted input; small, isolated, can land with or right after core.
- **Excluded (with rationale):** see Non-goals.

## Security — threat model (the session JSONL is attacker-controlled input in practice)

- **Attacker-controlled inputs:** the session file itself. ANY process sharing it — agent-side python (the incident), a skewed helper binary, disk corruption, hand edits, other apps in the group container — can append arbitrary bytes at any time. Gateway quota JSON (sites 4) is network-controlled. The reader is the boundary fa owns; the writers are not.
- **Impossible-by-construction:** no parse of persisted bytes may throw across the run boundary (INV1) — implemented by deleting the throwing path, not by a top-level catch that still lets partial state escape.
- **Quarantine framing:** a malformed record is untrusted DATA. It is excluded from context; the report carries a bounded literal excerpt for diagnosis, never re-embedded into model-visible context beyond the single system-authored note.
- **Instruction hierarchy:** only real user input authorizes anything. A quarantined record's contents can never issue instructions — they never re-enter context; the note itself is system-authored (file/line/id/excerpt), not record-authored prose.
- **Exfiltration gate:** the quarantine report and repair report go to the CLI/stderr/fa.log only — they trigger no provider calls and no telemetry of record contents.
- **Defense in depth:** layer 1 the non-throwing parser, layer 2 quarantine exclusion from context, layer 3 repair tooling, layer 4 golden REG against valid-input drift. Model obedience is hygiene; the non-throwing parser + quarantine IS the boundary.
- **Fixtures:** the incident record becomes a test fixture verbatim (record id `01a1d4b0-c9b6-709b-80c2-3cd97501a715`, timestamp `2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ`, deep line position) — treated strictly as data.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — `parseRecordTimestamp` returns a value with `degraded` set for EVERY fixture (`.fZ`, empty string, `<garbage>`, numeric epoch string, valid ISO, valid ISO+Z+micros) and throws on none. (UT hook: pure-function corpus test.)
- **AC2** — Valid ISO strings decode to the EXACT `DateTime` the bare parse produced before (identical to the microsecond) — zero drift. (UT hook: golden vs `DateTime.parse`.)
- **AC3** — A session file containing the incident poison record at a deep position resumes, submits, triggers auto-compaction, and completes the turn — no `stop=error`, no provider-error render. (IT hook: windowed storage harness; the 11:29:54 log sequence must not reproduce.)
- **AC4** — The poison record is quarantined: absent from `getBranch()`/context; the file is byte-identical after the run (hash equal). (IT hook: branch assertion + file hash.)
- **AC5** — The one-time report names file path, line number, record id, and raw timestamp value, and appears exactly once per process across ≥3 turns. (IT hook: stderr/log capture.)
- **AC6** — `fa session repair` scan mode lists the poison record (file+line+id+raw value) on a large synthetic file; a repair pass preserves the original at `<file>.bak` (rotating an existing `.bak` to `.bak1`); the repaired file resumes with no quarantine report for the fixed record. (E2E hook: CLI run.)
- **AC7** — Boot behavior: a poison record OUTSIDE the boot window still never fails resume; a poison record INSIDE the boot window also never fails boot (degrade + quarantine at window parse). `resume_timing` logging (`window_records`, `has_older`) unchanged. (IT hooks, positive + negative.)

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero drift for valid input

- `UT-1` (AC1) — fixture corpus: `.fZ`, `''`, `<garbage>`, `'1773000000000'` (numeric epoch), valid ISO, valid ISO+Z+micros → no-throw + placeholder + `degraded=true`.
- `UT-2` (AC2) — NEGATIVE for drift: valid corpus (incl. writer-canonical forms) parses to the exact same value as bare `DateTime.parse`; zero drift.
- `UT-3` (F1) — root-cause pin: bare `DateTime.parse('2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ')` throws FormatException (documents WHY); `parseRecordTimestamp` on the same input does not (the fix).
- `UT-4` (F2) — id-contract pin: `generateSessionEntryId` output matches the 8-char tail contract (sampled ≥10k ids, no full uuidv7); documents the incident forensics. Runtime does NOT gate on record-id shape (excluded from scope).
- `UT-5` (AC5) — report line format contains file, line, record id, bounded raw value; `UT-6` (AC5) — dedupe: same record across 3 decodes → one report; `UT-7` (E9) — flood cap: N poison records → capped lines + count summary.
- `UT-8` (second tier, AC1/AC2) — `ProviderQuota.fromJson` with `.fZ` `resetsAt`/`updatedAt` → no throw, placeholder + flag; `session_repo` `createdAtIso` same.
- `IT-1` (AC3/4/5) — windowed resume where the poison record sits OUTSIDE the boot window (deep position, `defaultChunkRecords=200`); submit triggers compaction → run completes, poison quarantined, warning names file+line+record id; file hash unchanged.
- `IT-2` (AC7) — poison INSIDE the boot window: boot succeeds, degrade + quarantine (pre-fix this fails boot — the incident only survived boot because the record was deep).
- `IT-3` (AC1 path 1) — poison in the session HEADER timestamp; `IT-4` (AC1 path 3) — poison hitting the `parseShallowCustomRecord` raw scan (small `<64 KiB` custom line).
- `IT-5` (E7) — quarantined record is the `parentId` of live records: children still usable, branch walk stable.
- `E2E-1` (AC3) — resume of a real poisoned session file: fixture generator derives from the incident (same record id, same timestamp, same deep position in a multi-hundred-MB synthetic file).
- `E2E-2` (AC6, F4) — `fa session repair` on that file: scan lists the record; repair keeps `.bak`; post-repair resume clean; the pre-fix crash-loop signature (two byte-identical ~300 ms `stop=error` turns) is impossible to reproduce.
- `REG-1` (INV4/AC2) — golden sessions across old versions parse byte-identically: same DateTime values, same record counts, same context projection — zero behavior change for valid input.
- `REG-2` (INV4) — semantic-drift property: random valid-ISO corpus through `parseRecordTimestamp` ≡ old bare parse, always.
- **CI merge rule: a red REG job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**

### Pinned platform facts (each with positive + negative test)

- **F1** — Dart `DateTime.parse` throws FormatException on a non-digit fraction (`2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ`). Positive: UT-3 bare-parse-throws pin. Negative: UT-1/UT-3 same input through `parseRecordTimestamp` returns placeholder. Degradation: placeholder + degraded flag.
- **F2** — `generateSessionEntryId` (`session_storage.dart:161–172`) emits the 8-char uuidv7 tail; the full-uuidv7 fallback fires only after 100 collisions (never in practice). Positive: UT-4 shape pin. Negative: a foreign full-uuidv7 record id (the incident's) is detectable by this contract — but this card deliberately builds NO runtime gate on it (see Non-goals); UT-4 documents forensics only.
- **F3** — the boot windowed reader parses ~the last 200 records (`defaultChunkRecords = 200`, `lib/src/session/session_chunk_reader.dart:26`; `resume_timing ... window_records=... has_older=...` logged at `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart:251–253`; resident default `3×200`). Positive: IT-1 resume of a deep-poison file logs `window_records=200 has_older=true` and succeeds. Negative: IT-2 poison inside the window must ALSO survive boot after this card.
- **F4** — crash-loop evidence: two byte-identical ~300 ms `stop=error` turns (fa.log 11:29:54 and 11:30:12), preceded by `auto-compact start tokens=195030`. Positive: E2E-2 asserts the signature cannot be reproduced. Negative: E2E valid-session timing/behavior unchanged.

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — poison in the header (line 1): degrade header timestamp, resume works.
- **E2** — multiple poison records: each quarantined, each reported once.
- **E3** — poison inside vs outside the boot window (E2 of the amplifier): both non-fatal.
- **E4** — numeric-epoch string: degraded, NOT invented into an epoch parse (no grammar widening).
- **E5** — exotic-but-valid ISO (offset forms, 6-digit fractions): accepted exactly as today (no narrowing either).

# gh-2178: [GOAL] Unbrickable session reads — malformed persisted records quarantine themselves, never crash the run (FormatException on hand-appended obligations_ledger)

## Description

## Goal — Unbrickable session reads (v1, first draft)

One sentence: **fa sessions become unbrickable from persisted input — one malformed record quarantines itself with a named, repairable report instead of crashing every turn.**

Today, a single foreign record with a malformed timestamp bricks a 664 MB session: every turn dies within ~300 ms behind a misclassified "provider error". What changes: every parse site that decodes persisted session bytes routes through one tolerant timestamp parser; a record that fails decode is quarantined (excluded from context building, preserved byte-verbatim in the file) with a one-time report naming file, line, record id, and the raw field value; `fa session repair` gains a scan mode that finds and reports such records. Why now: the 2026-11-13→14 incident below is a real, fully-diagnosed instance of the class — and the class is open-ended (any process that touches the JSONL can land it).

## Incident (2026-11-13 → 2026-11-14) — real; every value below is test data

Session `01a0ca2d-783a-78a0-8217-0533f83f8912` of project `~/git/aiin` (aiin), file `2026-09-22T20-32-52-666532_01a0ca2d-783a-78a0-8217-0533f83f8912.jsonl`, 664,905,120 bytes, 37,467 records, under `~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/--Users-uladzimir-klyshevich-git-aiin--/`.

- **2026-11-13 14:29** — a headless `fa --session <name> --prompt-file /tmp/close_aiin_obligations.md` run (launched from the YoLoIT desktop app) shared the SAME session file with the live interactive instance; it closed 32 `obligations_ledger` obligations.
- **14:35:18** — a synthetic `obligations_ledger` custom record was appended DIRECTLY to the JSONL, bypassing the Session API, with `"timestamp": "2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ"` (line 36,937 of the file).
- **Proof the writer was foreign (NOT fa's session layer):**
  - (a) record id `01a1d4b0-c9b6-709b-80c2-3cd97501a715` is a FULL uuidv7; fa's `generateSessionEntryId` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:161–172` on origin/main) always emits the 8-char uuidv7 TAIL (full uuidv7 only after a 100-collision fallback that never fires in practice); the uuidv7 embedded ms decode to 2026-11-13 14:35:18.198 — the same second as the mangled timestamp;
  - (b) the literal `.fZ` fraction (a strftime-style `.%fZ` typo: local clock digits + literal `f` + `Z`) exists in NO fa tag v1.0.715..v1.0.724, NOT on origin/main, and NOT in the compiled YoLoIT.app AOT snapshot (all greps verified empty);
  - (c) 21 s later (record at line 36,943) the interactive session's own bash tool result shows an agent-side python ledger analysis printing `latest ts 2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ` — python was live on this file inside the agent flow.
- **2026-11-14** — user updated fa 1.0.717 → 1.0.724.
- **11:29:19 boot** — resume SUCCEEDS: the windowed reader parsed only the last 200 records (fa.log: `resume_timing open ... window_records=200 ... has_older=true`); the malformed record at position 36,937 is outside that window → masked at boot.
- **11:29:54 first submit** — `auto-compact start tokens=195030` → compaction walks the full branch (`session.getBranch()`, `lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart:1610`, `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:847`) → `SessionRecord.fromJson` bare `DateTime.parse('2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ')` (`lib/src/session/session_record.dart:165`) → FormatException → rendered as `provider error raw ... FormatException: Invalid date format / 2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_run.dart:255` `_renderProviderError` via `_handleRunError`) → `stop=error` within 300 ms.
- **11:30:12 second submit** — byte-identical crash. EVERY subsequent turn repeats → the 664 MB session is bricked. User-visible clip: `error: FormatException: Invalid date format` / `2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ`.

## Mechanism (one sentence, verbatim)

> A foreign hand-appended session record with a malformed timestamp hits the bare `DateTime.parse` in `SessionRecord.fromJson`, so the auto-compactor's full-branch walk throws a FormatException that surfaces as a provider error and kills every turn — amplified by the boot windowed reader (resume fine, first submit dead), the provider-error misclassification (blames the network/update, not the record), and the absence of any corrupt-record quarantine or repair (`session_repair.dart` fixes tool pairing only).

## Why this framing

- **RETRACTED: "1.0.717 → 1.0.724 regression".** The bare `DateTime.parse` is identical in both tags; the update merely re-opened the session one day after the poison landed. Framing it as a regression sends the fix hunting in the wrong diff. (The retraction is why this card pins against origin/main, not a tag pair.)
- **RETRACTED: "provider/network failure".** The error surfaced through the provider-error renderer (`agent_cli_run.dart:255`), so the user blamed the model endpoint and the update. The failure is 100% local, in fa's own record decode, and reproducible with the network unplugged.
- **RETRACTED: "fix the writer".** Hardening one writer (the incident's python) does nothing for the next one: any process sharing the file can append arbitrary bytes. The reader is the only boundary fa owns (see threat model).
- **Kept: "unbrickable from persisted input".** The end state is about the session surviving its own file, not about any specific poison. Timestamp is the demonstrated instance; the protocol built here (tolerant decode → quarantine → named report → repair) is the shape.

## Architecture

Named protocol **`parseRecordTimestamp`**: one pure function, the ONLY way persisted-input timestamps decode.

```
parseRecordTimestamp(raw: String) → (DateTime, degraded: bool)
  1. strict ISO parse first — EXACTLY the grammar bare DateTime.parse accepts today
     (no widening, no narrowing: offset forms, Z, fractional digits — unchanged)
  2. on FormatException → deterministic placeholder DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(0)
     + degraded=true
  3. NEVER throws — no throwing path exists in the API
```

Call sites (core scope), all on origin/main:

- `lib/src/session/session_record.dart:100` — header `timestamp` (`SessionHeader.fromJson`).
- `lib/src/session/session_record.dart:165` — record `timestamp` (`SessionRecord.fromJson`; the crash site).
- `lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:279` — `parseShallowCustomRecord` raw scan. Note: this site already swallows the exception (`on Object { return null; }`) but its contract is "fall back to full decode" — which lands on the bare parse at `:165` and throws anyway. After this card it degrades in place; the fallback remains for other malformed-prefix classes.

**Quarantine + report** (runtime, read-time only — the file is never rewritten by the reader):

- A record whose timestamp degraded is excluded from context building and branch walks (`getBranch`, `buildContextMessages`) but preserved **byte-verbatim** in the file.
- One-time report per malformed record per process: file path, line number, record id, raw field value (bounded excerpt, single line). Surfaces as a CLI warning + fa.log diagnostic; deduped so a repeated turn cannot spam it.
- If a quarantined record is a tree parent of live records, its children remain usable (the record is treated as absent — the same semantics `repairSessionLedgers` already gives dropped records).

**Repair scan mode** (`fa session repair`):

- Gains a scan/report pass that walks the whole file with the existing line scanner and lists every malformed record (file + line + record id + raw value), including ones outside any boot window.
- Optional surgical fix reuses the byte-verbatim surgery + backup infra from `repairSessionLedgers` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`): original preserved at `<path>.bak`, rotated `.bak` → `.bak1` on a second pass, temp `$path.repairing`, writer-lock guard refused under a live writer.
- Today's repair is conservative by construction (unknown custom types and unparseable lines are KEPT) — which is exactly why the poison record survives a repair pass untouched. The scan mode makes it visible instead.

Flow, before → after:

```
boot (windowed ~200 recs: defaultChunkRecords=200)      submit / auto-compact
        |                                                       |
  WindowedSessionStorage                              compactSession ─ session.getBranch()  (FULL branch)
  last 200 records decode                                     |
        |                                             SessionRecord.fromJson
  poison at line 36,937 OUTSIDE window                        |                     |
  → masked, resume OK                                bare DateTime.parse    parseRecordTimestamp (NEW)
                                                           |                     |
                                                    FormatException      strict ok │ FormatException
                                                           |                |            |
                                                    provider error      exact      placeholder + degraded
                                                    stop=error ~300ms   DateTime          |
                                                           |                |        QUARANTINE: skip context,
                                                           v                v        keep bytes verbatim,
                                                    EVERY turn dies    (unchanged)  1× report (file, line,
                                                                                   id, raw value)
```

Invariants:

- **INV1** — no parse of persisted session bytes may throw across the run boundary. Impossible-by-construction: the throwing API for timestamp decode no longer exists (not "caught somewhere", removed).
- **INV2** — the runtime reader never mutates the session file; the only rewriter is `fa session repair` with `.bak` preservation.
- **INV3** — the quarantine report fires at most once per malformed record per process, regardless of turn count.
- **INV4** — valid timestamps decode to the exact `DateTime` the bare parse produced before (bit-identical; golden REG).

## Capability surface (all persisted-input parse sites → our shape)

| # | Parse site (pinned on origin/main) | Input | Today | This card |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `lib/src/session/session_record.dart:100` | header `timestamp` | bare `DateTime.parse` → FormatException kills resume | `parseRecordTimestamp` + degrade |
| 2 | `lib/src/session/session_record.dart:165` | record `timestamp` | bare parse → FormatException kills every turn (the incident) | `parseRecordTimestamp` + **quarantine + report** |
| 3 | `lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:279` | shallow custom-record raw scan | swallows, falls back to full decode where #2 throws | `parseRecordTimestamp`, degrade in place |
| 4 | `lib/src/providers/quota.dart:97/:101` | gateway JSON `resetsAt` / `updatedAt` | bare parse (network-controlled input) | **second tier**: same parser, degrade |
| 5 | `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:1524` | listing index `createdAtIso` | bare parse | **second tier**: same parser, degrade |

### Tolerant timestamp decode (subject: every persisted/network timestamp fa reads)
Strict-first, deterministic placeholder on failure, never throws. The accepted grammar does not change in either direction (INV4) — this is survivability, not leniency.

### Quarantine + report (subject: malformed session records)
Excluded from context/branch walks; bytes preserved verbatim; one-time named report (file, line, record id, raw value); flood-capped (many poison records → per-record lines up to a cap, then a count summary).

### Repair scan mode (subject: the session file on disk)
Whole-file scan, finds poison outside any window, reports it, optional byte-verbatim surgical fix with `.bak` rotation; refused under a live writer.

### Tiering
- **Core (this card):** sites 1–3, quarantine + report, repair scan mode.
- **Second tier (in-card, opt-in):** sites 4–5 — same-class hardening of sibling bare `DateTime.parse` on untrusted input; small, isolated, can land with or right after core.
- **Excluded (with rationale):** see Non-goals.

## Security — threat model (the session JSONL is attacker-controlled input in practice)

- **Attacker-controlled inputs:** the session file itself. ANY process sharing it — agent-side python (the incident), a skewed helper binary, disk corruption, hand edits, other apps in the group container — can append arbitrary bytes at any time. Gateway quota JSON (sites 4) is network-controlled. The reader is the boundary fa owns; the writers are not.
- **Impossible-by-construction:** no parse of persisted bytes may throw across the run boundary (INV1) — implemented by deleting the throwing path, not by a top-level catch that still lets partial state escape.
- **Quarantine framing:** a malformed record is untrusted DATA. It is excluded from context; the report carries a bounded literal excerpt for diagnosis, never re-embedded into model-visible context beyond the single system-authored note.
- **Instruction hierarchy:** only real user input authorizes anything. A quarantined record's contents can never issue instructions — they never re-enter context; the note itself is system-authored (file/line/id/excerpt), not record-authored prose.
- **Exfiltration gate:** the quarantine report and repair report go to the CLI/stderr/fa.log only — they trigger no provider calls and no telemetry of record contents.
- **Defense in depth:** layer 1 the non-throwing parser, layer 2 quarantine exclusion from context, layer 3 repair tooling, layer 4 golden REG against valid-input drift. Model obedience is hygiene; the non-throwing parser + quarantine IS the boundary.
- **Fixtures:** the incident record becomes a test fixture verbatim (record id `01a1d4b0-c9b6-709b-80c2-3cd97501a715`, timestamp `2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ`, deep line position) — treated strictly as data.

What changes: every parse site that decodes persisted session bytes routes through one tolerant timestamp parser; a record that fails decode is quarantined (excluded from context building, preserved byte-verbatim in the file) with a one-time report naming file, line, record id, and the raw field value; `fa session repair` gains a scan mode that finds and reports such records. Why now: the 2026-11-13→14 incident below is a real, fully-diagnosed instance of the class — and the class is open-ended (any process that touches the JSONL can land it).

## Incident (2026-11-13 → 2026-11-14) — real; every value below is test data

Session `01a0ca2d-783a-78a0-8217-0533f83f8912` of project `~/git/aiin` (aiin), file `2026-09-22T20-32-52-666532_01a0ca2d-783a-78a0-8217-0533f83f8912.jsonl`, 664,905,120 bytes, 37,467 records, under `~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/--Users-uladzimir-klyshevich-git-aiin--/`.

- **2026-11-13 14:29** — a headless `fa --session <name> --prompt-file /tmp/close_aiin_obligations.md` run (launched from the YoLoIT desktop app) shared the SAME session file with the live interactive instance; it closed 32 `obligations_ledger` obligations.
- **14:35:18** — a synthetic `obligations_ledger` custom record was appended DIRECTLY to the JSONL, bypassing the Session API, with `"timestamp": "2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ"` (line 36,937 of the file).
- **Proof the writer was foreign (NOT fa's session layer):**
  - (a) record id `01a1d4b0-c9b6-709b-80c2-3cd97501a715` is a FULL uuidv7; fa's `generateSessionEntryId` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:161–172` on origin/main) always emits the 8-char uuidv7 TAIL (full uuidv7 only after a 100-collision fallback that never fires in practice); the uuidv7 embedded ms decode to 2026-11-13 14:35:18.198 — the same second as the mangled timestamp;
  - (b) the literal `.fZ` fraction (a strftime-style `.%fZ` typo: local clock digits + literal `f` + `Z`) exists in NO fa tag v1.0.715..v1.0.724, NOT on origin/main, and NOT in the compiled YoLoIT.app AOT snapshot (all greps verified empty);
  - (c) 21 s later (record at line 36,943) the interactive session's own bash tool result shows an agent-side python ledger analysis printing `latest ts 2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ` — python was live on this file inside the agent flow.
- **2026-11-14** — user updated fa 1.0.717 → 1.0.724.
- **11:29:19 boot** — resume SUCCEEDS: the windowed reader parsed only the last 200 records (fa.log: `resume_timing open ... window_records=200 ... has_older=true`); the malformed record at position 36,937 is outside that window → masked at boot.
- **11:29:54 first submit** — `auto-compact start tokens=195030` → compaction walks the full branch (`session.getBranch()`, `lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart:1610`, `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:847`) → `SessionRecord.fromJson` bare `DateTime.parse('2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ')` (`lib/src/session/session_record.dart:165`) → FormatException → rendered as `provider error raw ... FormatException: Invalid date format / 2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_run.dart:255` `_renderProviderError` via `_handleRunError`) → `stop=error` within 300 ms.
- **11:30:12 second submit** — byte-identical crash. EVERY subsequent turn repeats → the 664 MB session is bricked. User-visible clip: `error: FormatException: Invalid date format` / `2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ`.

## Mechanism (one sentence, verbatim)

> A foreign hand-appended session record with a malformed timestamp hits the bare `DateTime.parse` in `SessionRecord.fromJson`, so the auto-compactor's full-branch walk throws a FormatException that surfaces as a provider error and kills every turn — amplified by the boot windowed reader (resume fine, first submit dead), the provider-error misclassification (blames the network/update, not the record), and the absence of any corrupt-record quarantine or repair (`session_repair.dart` fixes tool pairing only).

## Why this framing

- **RETRACTED: "1.0.717 → 1.0.724 regression".** The bare `DateTime.parse` is identical in both tags; the update merely re-opened the session one day after the poison landed. Framing it as a regression sends the fix hunting in the wrong diff. (The retraction is why this card pins against origin/main, not a tag pair.)
- **RETRACTED: "provider/network failure".** The error surfaced through the provider-error renderer (`agent_cli_run.dart:255`), so the user blamed the model endpoint and the update. The failure is 100% local, in fa's own record decode, and reproducible with the network unplugged.
- **RETRACTED: "fix the writer".** Hardening one writer (the incident's python) does nothing for the next one: any process sharing the file can append arbitrary bytes. The reader is the only boundary fa owns (see threat model).
- **Kept: "unbrickable from persisted input".** The end state is about the session surviving its own file, not about any specific poison. Timestamp is the demonstrated instance; the protocol built here (tolerant decode → quarantine → named report → repair) is the shape.

## Architecture

Named protocol **`parseRecordTimestamp`**: one pure function, the ONLY way persisted-input timestamps decode.

```
parseRecordTimestamp(raw: String) → (DateTime, degraded: bool)
  1. strict ISO parse first — EXACTLY the grammar bare DateTime.parse accepts today
     (no widening, no narrowing: offset forms, Z, fractional digits — unchanged)
  2. on FormatException → deterministic placeholder DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(0)
     + degraded=true
  3. NEVER throws — no throwing path exists in the API
```

Call sites (core scope), all on origin/main:

- `lib/src/session/session_record.dart:100` — header `timestamp` (`SessionHeader.fromJson`).
- `lib/src/session/session_record.dart:165` — record `timestamp` (`SessionRecord.fromJson`; the crash site).
- `lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:279` — `parseShallowCustomRecord` raw scan. Note: this site already swallows the exception (`on Object { return null; }`) but its contract is "fall back to full decode" — which lands on the bare parse at `:165` and throws anyway. After this card it degrades in place; the fallback remains for other malformed-prefix classes.

**Quarantine + report** (runtime, read-time only — the file is never rewritten by the reader):

- A record whose timestamp degraded is excluded from context building and branch walks (`getBranch`, `buildContextMessages`) but preserved **byte-verbatim** in the file.
- One-time report per malformed record per process: file path, line number, record id, raw field value (bounded excerpt, single line). Surfaces as a CLI warning + fa.log diagnostic; deduped so a repeated turn cannot spam it.
- If a quarantined record is a tree parent of live records, its children remain usable (the record is treated as absent — the same semantics `repairSessionLedgers` already gives dropped records).

**Repair scan mode** (`fa session repair`):

- Gains a scan/report pass that walks the whole file with the existing line scanner and lists every malformed record (file + line + record id + raw value), including ones outside any boot window.
- Optional surgical fix reuses the byte-verbatim surgery + backup infra from `repairSessionLedgers` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`): original preserved at `<path>.bak`, rotated `.bak` → `.bak1` on a second pass, temp `$path.repairing`, writer-lock guard refused under a live writer.
- Today's repair is conservative by construction (unknown custom types and unparseable lines are KEPT) — which is exactly why the poison record survives a repair pass untouched. The scan mode makes it visible instead.

Flow, before → after:

```
boot (windowed ~200 recs: defaultChunkRecords=200)      submit / auto-compact
        |                                                       |
  WindowedSessionStorage                              compactSession ─ session.getBranch()  (FULL branch)
  last 200 records decode                                     |
        |                                             SessionRecord.fromJson
  poison at line 36,937 OUTSIDE window                        |                     |
  → masked, resume OK                                bare DateTime.parse    parseRecordTimestamp (NEW)
                                                           |                     |
                                                    FormatException      strict ok │ FormatException
                                                           |                |            |
                                                    provider error      exact      placeholder + degraded
                                                    stop=error ~300ms   DateTime          |
                                                           |                |        QUARANTINE: skip context,
                                                           v                v        keep bytes verbatim,
                                                    EVERY turn dies    (unchanged)  1× report (file, line,
                                                                                   id, raw value)
```

Invariants:

- **INV1** — no parse of persisted session bytes may throw across the run boundary. Impossible-by-construction: the throwing API for timestamp decode no longer exists (not "caught somewhere", removed).
- **INV2** — the runtime reader never mutates the session file; the only rewriter is `fa session repair` with `.bak` preservation.
- **INV3** — the quarantine report fires at most once per malformed record per process, regardless of turn count.
- **INV4** — valid timestamps decode to the exact `DateTime` the bare parse produced before (bit-identical; golden REG).

## Capability surface (all persisted-input parse sites → our shape)

| # | Parse site (pinned on origin/main) | Input | Today | This card |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `lib/src/session/session_record.dart:100` | header `timestamp` | bare `DateTime.parse` → FormatException kills resume | `parseRecordTimestamp` + degrade |
| 2 | `lib/src/session/session_record.dart:165` | record `timestamp` | bare parse → FormatException kills every turn (the incident) | `parseRecordTimestamp` + **quarantine + report** |
| 3 | `lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:279` | shallow custom-record raw scan | swallows, falls back to full decode where #2 throws | `parseRecordTimestamp`, degrade in place |
| 4 | `lib/src/providers/quota.dart:97/:101` | gateway JSON `resetsAt` / `updatedAt` | bare parse (network-controlled input) | **second tier**: same parser, degrade |
| 5 | `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:1524` | listing index `createdAtIso` | bare parse | **second tier**: same parser, degrade |

### Tolerant timestamp decode (subject: every persisted/network timestamp fa reads)
Strict-first, deterministic placeholder on failure, never throws. The accepted grammar does not change in either direction (INV4) — this is survivability, not leniency.

### Quarantine + report (subject: malformed session records)
Excluded from context/branch walks; bytes preserved verbatim; one-time named report (file, line, record id, raw value); flood-capped (many poison records → per-record lines up to a cap, then a count summary).

### Repair scan mode (subject: the session file on disk)
Whole-file scan, finds poison outside any window, reports it, optional byte-verbatim surgical fix with `.bak` rotation; refused under a live writer.

### Tiering
- **Core (this card):** sites 1–3, quarantine + report, repair scan mode.
- **Second tier (in-card, opt-in):** sites 4–5 — same-class hardening of sibling bare `DateTime.parse` on untrusted input; small, isolated, can land with or right after core.
- **Excluded (with rationale):** see Non-goals.

## Security — threat model (the session JSONL is attacker-controlled input in practice)

- **Attacker-controlled inputs:** the session file itself. ANY process sharing it — agent-side python (the incident), a skewed helper binary, disk corruption, hand edits, other apps in the group container — can append arbitrary bytes at any time. Gateway quota JSON (sites 4) is network-controlled. The reader is the boundary fa owns; the writers are not.
- **Impossible-by-construction:** no parse of persisted bytes may throw across the run boundary (INV1) — implemented by deleting the throwing path, not by a top-level catch that still lets partial state escape.
- **Quarantine framing:** a malformed record is untrusted DATA. It is excluded from context; the report carries a bounded literal excerpt for diagnosis, never re-embedded into model-visible context beyond the single system-authored note.
- **Instruction hierarchy:** only real user input authorizes anything. A quarantined record's contents can never issue instructions — they never re-enter context; the note itself is system-authored (file/line/id/excerpt), not record-authored prose.
- **Exfiltration gate:** the quarantine report and repair report go to the CLI/stderr/fa.log only — they trigger no provider calls and no telemetry of record contents.
- **Defense in depth:** layer 1 the non-throwing parser, layer 2 quarantine exclusion from context, layer 3 repair tooling, layer 4 golden REG against valid-input drift. Model obedience is hygiene; the non-throwing parser + quarantine IS the boundary.
- **Fixtures:** the incident record becomes a test fixture verbatim (record id `01a1d4b0-c9b6-709b-80c2-3cd97501a715`, timestamp `2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ`, deep line position) — treated strictly as data.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — `parseRecordTimestamp` returns a value with `degraded` set for EVERY fixture (`.fZ`, empty string, `<garbage>`, numeric epoch string, valid ISO, valid ISO+Z+micros) and throws on none. (UT hook: pure-function corpus test.)
- **AC2** — Valid ISO strings decode to the EXACT `DateTime` the bare parse produced before (identical to the microsecond) — zero drift. (UT hook: golden vs `DateTime.parse`.)
- **AC3** — A session file containing the incident poison record at a deep position resumes, submits, triggers auto-compaction, and completes the turn — no `stop=error`, no provider-error render. (IT hook: windowed storage harness; the 11:29:54 log sequence must not reproduce.)
- **AC4** — The poison record is quarantined: absent from `getBranch()`/context; the file is byte-identical after the run (hash equal). (IT hook: branch assertion + file hash.)
- **AC5** — The one-time report names file path, line number, record id, and raw timestamp value, and appears exactly once per process across ≥3 turns. (IT hook: stderr/log capture.)
- **AC6** — `fa session repair` scan mode lists the poison record (file+line+id+raw value) on a large synthetic file; a repair pass preserves the original at `<file>.bak` (rotating an existing `.bak` to `.bak1`); the repaired file resumes with no quarantine report for the fixed record. (E2E hook: CLI run.)
- **AC7** — Boot behavior: a poison record OUTSIDE the boot window still never fails resume; a poison record INSIDE the boot window also never fails boot (degrade + quarantine at window parse). `resume_timing` logging (`window_records`, `has_older`) unchanged. (IT hooks, positive + negative.)

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero drift for valid input

- `UT-1` (AC1) — fixture corpus: `.fZ`, `''`, `<garbage>`, `'1773000000000'` (numeric epoch), valid ISO, valid ISO+Z+micros → no-throw + placeholder + `degraded=true`.
- `UT-2` (AC2) — NEGATIVE for drift: valid corpus (incl. writer-canonical forms) parses to the exact same value as bare `DateTime.parse`; zero drift.
- `UT-3` (F1) — root-cause pin: bare `DateTime.parse('2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ')` throws FormatException (documents WHY); `parseRecordTimestamp` on the same input does not (the fix).
- `UT-4` (F2) — id-contract pin: `generateSessionEntryId` output matches the 8-char tail contract (sampled ≥10k ids, no full uuidv7); documents the incident forensics. Runtime does NOT gate on record-id shape (excluded from scope).
- `UT-5` (AC5) — report line format contains file, line, record id, bounded raw value; `UT-6` (AC5) — dedupe: same record across 3 decodes → one report; `UT-7` (E9) — flood cap: N poison records → capped lines + count summary.
- `UT-8` (second tier, AC1/AC2) — `ProviderQuota.fromJson` with `.fZ` `resetsAt`/`updatedAt` → no throw, placeholder + flag; `session_repo` `createdAtIso` same.
- `IT-1` (AC3/4/5) — windowed resume where the poison record sits OUTSIDE the boot window (deep position, `defaultChunkRecords=200`); submit triggers compaction → run completes, poison quarantined, warning names file+line+record id; file hash unchanged.
- `IT-2` (AC7) — poison INSIDE the boot window: boot succeeds, degrade + quarantine (pre-fix this fails boot — the incident only survived boot because the record was deep).
- `IT-3` (AC1 path 1) — poison in the session HEADER timestamp; `IT-4` (AC1 path 3) — poison hitting the `parseShallowCustomRecord` raw scan (small `<64 KiB` custom line).
- `IT-5` (E7) — quarantined record is the `parentId` of live records: children still usable, branch walk stable.
- `E2E-1` (AC3) — resume of a real poisoned session file: fixture generator derives from the incident (same record id, same timestamp, same deep position in a multi-hundred-MB synthetic file).
- `E2E-2` (AC6, F4) — `fa session repair` on that file: scan lists the record; repair keeps `.bak`; post-repair resume clean; the pre-fix crash-loop signature (two byte-identical ~300 ms `stop=error` turns) is impossible to reproduce.
- `REG-1` (INV4/AC2) — golden sessions across old versions parse byte-identically: same DateTime values, same record counts, same context projection — zero behavior change for valid input.
- `REG-2` (INV4) — semantic-drift property: random valid-ISO corpus through `parseRecordTimestamp` ≡ old bare parse, always.
- **CI merge rule: a red REG job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**

### Pinned platform facts (each with positive + negative test)

- **F1** — Dart `DateTime.parse` throws FormatException on a non-digit fraction (`2026-11-13T14:35:18.fZ`). Positive: UT-3 bare-parse-throws pin. Negative: UT-1/UT-3 same input through `parseRecordTimestamp` returns placeholder. Degradation: placeholder + degraded flag.
- **F2** — `generateSessionEntryId` (`session_storage.dart:161–172`) emits the 8-char uuidv7 tail; the full-uuidv7 fallback fires only after 100 collisions (never in practice). Positive: UT-4 shape pin. Negative: a foreign full-uuidv7 record id (the incident's) is detectable by this contract — but this card deliberately builds NO runtime gate on it (see Non-goals); UT-4 documents forensics only.
- **F3** — the boot windowed reader parses ~the last 200 records (`defaultChunkRecords = 200`, `lib/src/session/session_chunk_reader.dart:26`; `resume_timing ... window_records=... has_older=...` logged at `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart:251–253`; resident default `3×200`). Positive: IT-1 resume of a deep-poison file logs `window_records=200 has_older=true` and succeeds. Negative: IT-2 poison inside the window must ALSO survive boot after this card.
- **F4** — crash-loop evidence: two byte-identical ~300 ms `stop=error` turns (fa.log 11:29:54 and 11:30:12), preceded by `auto-compact start tokens=195030`. Positive: E2E-2 asserts the signature cannot be reproduced. Negative: E2E valid-session timing/behavior unchanged.

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — poison in the header (line 1): degrade header timestamp, resume works.
- **E2** — multiple poison records: each quarantined, each reported once.
- **E3** — poison inside vs outside the boot window (E2 of the amplifier): both non-fatal.
- **E4** — numeric-epoch string: degraded, NOT invented into an epoch parse (no grammar widening).
- **E5** — exotic-but-valid ISO (offset forms, 6-digit fractions): accepted exactly as today (no narrowing either).
- **E6** — repair under a live writer: refused, same guard as `repairSessionLedgers`.
- **E7** — quarantined record is a tree parent: children stay usable (treated-as-absent semantics).
- **E8** — poison in an old golden session: read-time degrade only, bytes never rewritten at runtime (REG corpus asserts no "silent fix").
- **E9** — report flood: capped per-record lines + count summary.
- **E10** — second submit is byte-identical to the first in inputs: post-fix, both succeed (the loop is gone at the root, not dodged).

## Non-goals

- **No supported ledger-close path** (tool/command) so agent flows never hand-edit the JSONL. This is THE amplifier of the incident — closing obligations demanded a flow that bypassed the Session API. It deserves its own card (Related Work).
- **Not fixing the external writer** — the incident's python/YoLoIT side is out of repo; and see the retracted framing above.
- **No compaction strategy change** — the full-branch walk stays; compaction work belongs to the auto-compact epic (#2095).
- **No record-id UUID validation** — the full-uuidv7 id is courtroom-grade forensics but a poor runtime gate (fa's own fallback can legally emit one; id shape is not the failure, the parse is).
- **No mojibake / other foreign-record classes** — timestamps are the demonstrated instance; the parser+quarantine protocol generalizes later.
- **No runtime file rewriting** — quarantine is read-time; `fa session repair` remains the only rewriter, always with `.bak`.

## Open questions

- **OQ1 — placeholder shape:** (a) epoch placeholder `DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(0)` + `degraded` flag — zero schema churn, orders poison at 1970; (b) nullable timestamp plumbed through `SessionRecord`/header — honest ordering, type churn across every record type. Recommend (a) for v1; (b) can follow without protocol change.
- **OQ2 — repair scan surface:** default report-only pre-pass inside `fa session repair` (dry-run is the existing pattern) vs a `--scan` flag vs a separate `fa session doctor`. Recommend the pre-pass.
- **OQ3 — does the quarantine report also land in the session file** as a custom record? Pro: durable audit; con: writes bytes into the very file being treated as poisoned. Recommend stderr + fa.log only in v1.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG

6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

For the repair scan: unknown-type lines with valid JSON decode... hmm, repair "keps unknown custom types" — CUSTOM types (type=custom), not unknown TYPES. An unknown `type` value line is torn at runtime. Not our concern. Finding = SessionRecord.fromJson succeeded + timestampDegraded. Exactly the runtime quarantine population.

So `quarantineFindingForLine` (rename: `sessionQuarantineFinding(line, ...)`) with a `_topLevelTimestampValue(line)` depth-scanner helper. Actually — wait, I realize I should double check something: the depth scan must handle escaped quotes inside strings ("\"). Standard mini-scanner: in-string flag, escape flag, depth tracking on { } [ ] only when not in-string. ~30 lines. OK.

Alternatively — MUCH simpler: only jsonDecode when `line.length < someBound`, else use shallowCustomHeader when applicable, else skip with a "deep custom line skipped" note? No — precision beats cleverness here; the depth scanner is simple and exact. Do the depth scan FIRST (cheap reject for lines without a depth-0 timestamp key — most lines DO have one though; it's the 4th field), tryParse the extracted raw (cheap accept for ~all valid lines), full decode ONLY when tryParse fails (rare) → finding or not.

Edge: the depth scanner extracts the value but the line is TORN JSON (no closing brace etc.) — tryParse may still parse the timestamp from a torn line (e.g. torn tail truncated mid-payload: timestamp valid → fast accept → no finding — correct-ish: a torn line is the .corupt path anyway, not a timestamp finding).

OK. Now — the runtime decode sites: do NOT use the depth scanner (they have real JSON already decoded). Only repair uses it.

One more thing to verify: `DateTime.tryParse` — exists in dart:core. Grammar identical to parse. 

And for `parseRecordTimestamp`: `DateTime.parse` on a valid string — note `DateTime.parse` can throw ArgumentError for... no — parse only throws FormatException per docs. To be strict per spec: `on FormatException`. INV1 says "NEVER throws — no throwing path exists in the API" — strictly, only FormatException can escape DateTime.parse; catching exactly FormatException preserves INV4 (no widening).

content.thinking: Found it: in my FIRST draft of the file I wrote `'$filePath\x00$recordId'` as the dedupe key — I literally embedded a NUL character in the source (I intended `\u000`-style separator, and the write tool inserted the actual byte rather than an escape). A NUL byte in source makes git treat the file as binary (no diff view for reviewers) — bad. Replace the NUL with a safe printable separator (e.g. a space — ids and paths don't contain spaces... paths CAN contain spaces. Better: use an unlikely literal like '\u000' escape in source code text: `'$filePath\u000$recordId'` — a Dart unicode escape, source stays ASCII-safe).

# the pub get above it — on an out-of-scope PR checkout/setup-dart/
      # pub get are all skipped (the fastpass keeps the leg green in
      # seconds) and an unconditional prewarm would red the required
      # contexts: the composite action file isn't even on disk without
      # checkout, and the script hard-fails without the pub get's package
      # config.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage

arguments.content:
### What changed
Malformed persisted session timestamps no longer brick the session: all persisted-input timestamp decodes now go through one strict-first, never-throwing parser (`parseRecordTimestamp`), and a record that still fails the strict parse quarantines itself — excluded from context building and branch walks, preserved byte-verbatim in the file, and reported once (file + line + record id + bounded raw value) instead of surfacing as a misclassified provider error on every turn.

### Key decisions
- One decode gate (`lib/src/session/record_quarantine.dart`): strict `DateTime.parse` grammar unchanged in both directions — no widening, no narrowing (valid input bit-identical); failures land on the deterministic epoch placeholder (OQ1 (a)) + a `timestampDegraded` flag carried on `SessionRecord`/`SessionHeader`.
- Quarantine is read-time only (INV2): the runtime reader never mutates the file — a poison record is not a torn line, so the open-time crash-heal rewrite does not fire. Children of a quarantined record stay usable (branch walks skip the node, continue through its parent).
- One-time report per malformed record per process (INV3): dedupe + 20-record flood cap in `SessionQuarantine` (E9), wired like `onRotationWarning` (bin boot stderr default; AgentCli notice channel + fa.log warn). Findings cross isolate-group boundaries via `SessionParseResult.quarantined` replay (statics are per-isolate).
- `fa session repair` gains the OQ2 scan pre-pass: every run lists malformed-timestamp records (deep positions included, exact physical line numbers) in the report; the real pass fixes them in place reusing the span surgery + `.bak`/`.bak1` rotation (only the fixed line's timestamp value changes). Superseded keep-latest snapshots are not counted as findings of the repaired file.
- Second tier: `ProviderQuota.fromJson` (gateway JSON, `timestampsDegraded` flag) and the repo listing-index `createdAtIso` serve degrade instead of failing the row/listing.
- Forensics preserved: `generateSessionEntryId` stays the 8-char uuidv7 tail pin (no runtime gate on id shape — IDs are data, treated strictly).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session/record_quarantine_test.dart            # 34 tests: parser corpus, report/dedupe/cap, walk exclusion, repair scan/fix, second tier
dart test test/session test/providers test/env --concurrency=8 # existing suites stay green
```

<details><summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LINE[JSONL record line] --> PARSE[parseSessionEntryLine / shallow]
  PARSE --> TS[parseRecordTimestamp]
  TS -->|strict ISO ok| OK[record as before — zero drift]
  TS -->|FormatException| DEG[epoch placeholder + timestampDegraded]
  DEG --> REP[SessionQuarantine.reportRecord — once per record per process]
  DEG --> WALK[getBranch / buildContextMessages: treated as absent, children usable]
  DEG --> FILE[file bytes untouched — fa session repair scan lists + fixes it]
```

</details>

## Summary

**gh-2178 — Unbrickable session reads** is implemented, tested, and committed (5 commits on `ai/gh-2178`, base 85c2a1a = origin/main exactly as pinned in `dev_base_head.txt`).

### What changed
- **`lib/src/session/record_quarantine.dart`** (new): `parseRecordTimestamp` — the one strict-first, never-throwing timestamp decode (valid input bit-identical, failures → deterministic epoch placeholder + `degraded`); `SessionQuarantine` — the once-per-record-per-process report (file + line + record id + bounded raw value, 20-record flood cap); the repair-scan line finder (exact depth-0 timestamp extraction, no full decode on the hot path).
- **Decode sites routed**: `SessionHeader.fromJson`, `SessionRecord.fromJson` (the incident's crash site), `parseShallowCustomRecord` (raw scan), plus second tier `ProviderQuota.fromJson` and the repo listing-index `createdAtIso`. Records carry `timestampDegraded`; findings cross isolate boundaries via `SessionParseResult.quarantined` replay.
- **Quarantine**: degraded records are excluded from `getPathToRoot`/context builds (treated as absent, children stay usable); the runtime reader never mutates the file (not a torn line — no crash-heal rewrite); wired to stderr (bin boot) + CLI notice channel + fa.log warn.
- **`fa session repair` scan mode**: every run now lists malformed-timestamp records (deep positions included, exact physical line numbers); the real pass fixes them in place via the existing span surgery + `.bak`/`.bak1` rotation, byte-verbatim everywhere except the fixed line's timestamp.
- 34 new tests in `test/session/record_quarantine_test.dart` covering the AC/UT/IT/F/E/REG matrix (corpus, zero-drift golden + 500-case property loop, report format/dedupe/cap, windowed boot inside/outside the window, walk exclusion, file immutability, repair scan/fix/dry-run/conservatism, multi-poison, second tier).
